program_name: "Master in Smart Sustainable Agriculture Systems in Mountain Areas" — the full official English name, used identically on the unibz programme page, in the 2026/27 brochure, in the 2026/27 admission-information PDF and in the header of both signed 2026/27 ranking-list decrees ("RANKING LIST — Admission to the Master in Smart Sustainable Agriculture Systems in Mountain Areas (LM-69)"). NO TRANSLATED NAME EXISTS. Unlike almost every other unibz degree, this programme has NO Italian and NO German page: requesting the Italian URL returns the notice "Siamo spiacenti, questa pagina non è disponibile in italiano. Vai alla pagina in inglese", and the English page itself carries the banner "This page is only available in English". Only the technical sub-pages (course offering, study plan) exist in IT/DE. Practically this means an applicant will never encounter an Italian title such as a hypothetical 'Sistemi agricoli intelligenti e sostenibili in aree montane' — the English name is the only name. NO OFFICIAL ABBREVIATION is published (contrast EMMA for Environmental Management of Mountain Areas). Internally unibz files it under the slug 'master-smart-sustainable-agriculture-systems-mountain-areas' and the PDF slug 'master-in-smart-sustainable-agriculture-systems-in-mountain-areas'. Third-party aggregators (Mastersportal, educations.com) sometimes shorten it to 'Smart Sustainable Agriculture Systems in Mountain Areas'. DELIVERED BY: the unibz Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences (Faculty Secretariat, Universitätsplatz 5 / piazza Università 5, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano; agriculture@unibz.it; +39 0471 017000). PEOPLE: Degree Course Director Prof. Christian Fischer; Student Representative in the Course Council Christian Giovannini; the 2026/27 Admission Committee was President Prof. Christian Fischer with members Prof. Andreas Gronauer and Dr. Thomas Zanon (all three digitally signed both ranking-list decrees). DO NOT CONFUSE IT with three neighbouring unibz programmes: (a) the Bachelor in Sustainable Agriculture and Forestry in Mountain Environments (L-25, the natural feeder degree); (b) the Master in Environmental Management of Mountain Areas / EMMA (LM-73, forestry-environmental, double degree with Innsbruck); (c) the Master in Horticultural Science (a joint programme with the University of Bologna, where applications are handled by Bologna, not unibz). All four sit in the same faculty and share the phrase 'mountain'.
level: Master — Italian 'laurea magistrale' (second-cycle degree), EQF/QF-EHEA level 7, 120 ECTS over 2 years / 4 semesters, degree class LM-69. Brochure 'At a Glance', verbatim: 'Degree class: LM-69 / ECTS credits: 120 / Duration of the course: 2 years'. ENTRY QUALIFICATION is a three-year bachelor degree; at enrolment the Diploma Supplement must state, verbatim, 'that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. AWARD: 'Dottore magistrale' in the LM-69 class; internationally equivalent to an MSc. ONWARD ACCESS: the degree gives access to Italian PhD programmes — unibz runs two directly relevant doctorates in the same faculty, the PhD in Mountain Environment and Agriculture and the PhD in Food Engineering and Biotechnology. PROFESSIONAL DIMENSION: LM-69 is one of the Italian degree classes that, after the state examination (esame di Stato), gives access to Section A of the Ordine dei Dottori Agronomi e Dottori Forestali (the 'Agronomist' profession). The unibz faculty runs 'Esami di stato' as a standing service and the programme page lists 'agronomists' first among career outcomes. [uncertain] Neither the 2026/27 brochure nor the admission-information PDF contains an explicit sentence stating that the programme prepares for the Italian professional qualification (EMMA's older manifesto did carry such a sentence). A candidate who intends to register with the Ordine should confirm the LM-69 → Section A pathway with the Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it) and with the relevant provincial Ordine, since professional-register access is governed by Italian ministerial tables, not by unibz. PART-TIME OPTION EXISTS, which is unusual and worth knowing: the programme page states that part-time enrolment 'allows you to reduce your study load' and that 'Students choose this option after enrollment (in October) and not during the application.' It is therefore not an admission variant, and choosing it does not change the admission procedure.
teaching_language: FULLY AND EXCLUSIVELY ENGLISH — this is NOT one of unibz's trilingual programmes, and unlike EMMA it does not even have a German-speaking partner year. Brochure 'At a Glance', verbatim: 'Courses will be taught in English'. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English.' The only admission language requirement is English at B2. There is NO German requirement, NO Italian requirement, NO third-language B1 threshold and NO exit/graduation language requirement anywhere in the 2026/27 documents. CORROBORATION FROM THE COURSE CATALOGUE: every single course in the published 2026/27 course offering is tagged 'EN' — Livestock production systems in mountain areas (47300), Mountain crop ecosystems (47301), Sustainable soil management (47302 with modules 47302A/47302B), Rural and agricultural development (47304 with 47304A/47304B), Smart design and planning of mountain livestock and grassland management technologies (47307), Agribusiness Management (47312), Smart agricultural technologies (47303), Plant and livestock health (47305), Transversal agricultural knowledge and skills (47309 with 47309A/47309B) and Informatics (47310). Two entries (Wildlife management in mountain areas 47311 and Forage crops and grassland management 47306) are displayed without a visible language tag in the catalogue listing, which is a display gap rather than a statement that they are taught in another language, since the governing documents say the official teaching language is English full stop. THE ONE PLACE WHERE OTHER LANGUAGES CAN APPEAR is the 24 ECTS of 'Free choice courses' in year 2 and, above all, the encouraged third semester at the University of Applied Sciences Weihenstephan-Triesdorf (HSWT) in Bavaria. HSWT is a German public university of applied sciences whose master teaching is substantially in German; an English-only student going there will have a narrower module menu and a German-speaking daily environment. This is an outbound-mobility consideration, not an admission or graduation requirement, and the exchange is explicitly optional ('Students are encouraged to spend the third semester at one of our partner universities'). [uncertain] unibz does not publish which HSWT modules are guaranteed in English for exchange students, nor the language of the free-choice catalogue offered each year in Bolzano. This is the single question an English-only applicant should put to the Degree Course Director (Prof. Christian Fischer) or the Faculty Secretariat before relying on the third-semester exchange. PRACTICAL NOTE ON LOCAL LANGUAGES: South Tyrolean agriculture itself operates in German and Italian. Field trips, farm visits (the programme page names visits at 'Kirnig - Südtiroler Edelpilze' and 'Solos Farm' and 'Field trip to local agricultural businesses') and internships with local growers will frequently involve German- or Italian-speaking practitioners, and the regional job market effectively requires German. That is a career and integration factor, not a curricular requirement. unibz Language Centre courses in German and Italian are available voluntarily.
campus: SINGLE CAMPUS: Bozen-Bolzano, Italy. Brochure 'At a Glance', verbatim: 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano'. The programme page repeats 'Campus located in Bozen-Bolzano'. This is a genuinely single-site programme for the taught core — unlike EMMA (Bolzano year 1 + Innsbruck year 2) or Energy Engineering (Bolzano + Trento). It is NOT delivered at Brixen-Bressanone, NOT at Bruneck-Brunico, and it is NOT a NOI Techpark-based programme, although the Faculty of Agricultural, Environmental and Food Sciences runs laboratories both in the city-centre campus and at NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano and students on lab-based theses may work there. ADDRESSES: the Faculty Secretariat that administers this programme is at Universitätsplatz 5 - piazza Università, 5, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano (Tel +39 0471 017000; agriculture@unibz.it; agriculture@pec.unibz.it). Opening hours as published: 'Mo, Wed: 10:00-12:00; Thu: 14:00-16:00; Tue, Fri: online only, 10:00 - 12:00'. The main university address is Universitätsplatz 1 - piazza Università 1. THE OPTIONAL SECOND LOCATION — THIRD SEMESTER ABROAD: 'Students are encouraged to spend the third semester at one of the programme's partner universities, in particular the University of Applied Sciences Weihenstephan-Triesdorf in Bavaria, Germany.' HSWT has two sites, Freising-Weihenstephan (near Munich) and Triesdorf (Middle Franconia); the agriculture faculty is at Triesdorf. Bolzano to Munich is roughly 3.5-4 hours by train. This mobility is ENCOURAGED, NOT COMPULSORY, and it is an exchange, not a double degree: nothing in the unibz documents promises a second diploma, an automatic place at HSWT, or a guaranteed English module set. [uncertain] The formal instrument behind the HSWT semester (Erasmus+ inter-institutional agreement vs. bilateral cooperation agreement), the number of places, the selection procedure and any grant amount are not published on the programme page and should be confirmed with the unibz International Relations Office. FIELD-BASED TEACHING: the programme is explicitly hands-on — 'Learning activities include theoretical classes, practical activities, field trips and internships' — so a significant part of contact time happens on South Tyrolean farms, grasslands, orchards and mountain sites rather than in the Bolzano lecture halls. CONTEXT FOR AN INTERNATIONAL APPLICANT: Bozen-Bolzano is an officially bilingual (German/Italian) city of about 107,000 in the Dolomites, roughly 2 hours from Innsbruck, 3.5 from Munich, 2 from Verona and 3 from Milan. unibz's own guidance puts living costs at 'at least € 800 per month' excluding tuition.
degree_class: LM-69 — 'Scienze e tecnologie agrarie' (Agricultural Science and Technology), the Italian ministerial second-cycle degree class established by D.M. 270/2004. Stated verbatim in the brochure 'At a Glance' ('Degree class: LM-69'), on the programme page, and in the title block of both signed 2026/27 ranking lists ('Admission to the Master in Smart Sustainable Agriculture Systems in Mountain Areas (LM-69)'). POSITION IN THE ITALIAN SYSTEM: LM-69 is the standard 'agricultural sciences' magistrale class, the natural second cycle above the bachelor class L-25 (Scienze e tecnologie agrarie, agroalimentari e forestali) — which is exactly why the entry requirements are written in terms of the L-25 credit sectors. It sits alongside, and is distinct from, LM-70 (food science and technology), LM-73 (forest and environmental sciences — the class of unibz's EMMA), LM-86 (animal science) and LM-7 (agricultural biotechnology). WHAT LM-69 BUYS YOU: (1) it is the ministerial class Italian professional bodies map to the agronomist profession, so after the esame di Stato it leads towards Section A of the Ordine dei Dottori Agronomi e Dottori Forestali; (2) it is recognised across the EU as a second-cycle qualification for public-sector and EU-agency recruitment. THE DOUBLE-ENROLMENT RULE keyed to the class, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: 'According to national regulations, you can enrol in a maximum of two programmes simultaneously, provided that they do not belong to the same class (e.g. LM-73 and LM-73) and differ in at least two-thirds of their content.' [uncertain] NOTE A COPY-PASTE ARTEFACT IN UNIBZ'S OWN TEXT: the example class given in this programme's admission-information PDF, brochure and ranking lists is 'LM-73 and LM-73' (and, in one paragraph of the Early Bird ranking list, 'LM-18/LM-18'), which are EMMA's and Computer Science's classes, not this programme's. The rule itself is a national rule and applies to LM-69 in the same way; the mismatched example is unibz boilerplate carried over from sibling documents, not a statement about this degree's class. ONE MORE UNIBZ-INTERNAL POINT: unibz's second LM-69-adjacent offering, the Master in Horticultural Science, is a joint programme administered by the University of Bologna. If you are comparing 'agriculture masters at unibz', check which institution actually admits and enrols you — for Smart Sustainable Agriculture Systems it is unibz itself, through the unibz Application Portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup .

FIRST INTAKE: academic year 2025/26, so the 2026/27 cohort is only the SECOND ever, and the first cohort will not graduate before the summer/autumn of 2027. CONVERGING EVIDENCE, since unibz publishes no 'new programme' badge: (1) INTERNET ARCHIVE — the Wayback Machine's first capture of the programme page is 14/02/2025, with NO snapshot in 2024 or earlier; captures then continue regularly through 2025 and 2026. A page that first appears in February 2025 is a page created for the March 2025 Early Bird window, i.e. the 2025/26 intake. (2) COURSE CATALOGUE — the academic-year selector on the course-offering page starts at 2025/26 (options: 2025/26, 2026/27, 2027/28); there is no 2024/25 offering. (3) NO GRADUATION DATA — unibz publishes per-class grade-statistics pages for established programmes (EMMA's '.../master-environmental-management-mountain-areas/grade-statistics-lm-73' returns HTTP 200); the equivalent '.../master-smart-sustainable-agriculture-systems-mountain-areas/grade-statistics-lm-69' returns HTTP 404. No graduates, therefore no distribution to publish. There is likewise no AlmaLaurea employability link on the programme page. (4) NO TRANSLATIONS — the Italian and German versions of the programme page do not exist ('Siamo spiacenti, questa pagina non è disponibile in italiano'), a classic marker of a page unibz has not yet processed through its full trilingual workflow. (5) COHORT SHAPE IN THE CATALOGUE — the 2026/27 offering contains all eleven first-year courses plus exactly one second-year course (Wildlife management in mountain areas, 47311), which is precisely what a programme in its second year of operation looks like. (6) CURRICULUM STILL BEING TUNED — the 6 CP second-semester course listed in the brochure study plan as 'Farm management and entrepreneurship' appears in the 2026/27 catalogue as 'Agribusiness Management' (code 47312, AGRI-01/A, Massimiliano Calvia), i.e. the plan was revised between the two cohorts. WHAT 'NEW' MEANS IN PRACTICE — THE UPSIDE: competition is extraordinarily low (see places_quotas and selection_scoring: 5 EU + 5 non-EU admitted in Early Bird against 25 + 10 places, and 3 EU admitted in the Late session), the faculty is investing in the programme, class sizes are tiny, and access to professors is close to one-to-one. THE DOWNSIDE, and it should be stated plainly: there is no alumni network, no graduate-employment statistics, no published grade distribution, no student-satisfaction data, no track record of how the free-choice year-2 catalogue actually works in practice, and no history of how many students really manage the HSWT semester. Timetables, elective menus and even course titles are still moving. An applicant who needs a proven programme with measurable outcomes should weigh EMMA (running since 2014, with published graduation-grade statistics) against this one. [uncertain] No unibz press release, Rector's decree or ministerial accreditation record confirming the exact activation year was located; the 2025/26 first-intake conclusion is an inference from the six independent signals above, all of which point the same way, rather than from a single official statement. Confirm with agriculture@unibz.it if the exact founding year matters.
majors_tracks_study_plans: ONE SINGLE STUDY PLAN. No majors, no tracks, no curricula, no separate admission codes and therefore no split quotas. Everybody admitted enters the same plan; the only individualisation is the 24 ECTS of free-choice courses in year 2 and the optional third-semester exchange. YEAR 1 — 60 ECTS, ENTIRELY COMPULSORY (brochure study plan, verbatim course titles and credits): 6 CP Livestock production systems in mountain areas; 3 CP Mountain crop ecosystems; 6 CP Sustainable soil management (= 3 CP Soil Protection + 3 CP Molecular Agroecology & Biochemistry); 6 CP Smart agricultural technologies; 9 CP Rural and agricultural development (= 6 CP Agricultural development, sustainable tourism and regional products + 3 CP Rural project design and management); 6 CP Plant and livestock health; 6 CP Forage crops and grassland management; 6 CP Smart design and planning of mountain livestock and grassland management technologies; 6 CP Farm management and entrepreneurship; 5 CP Transversal agricultural knowledge and skills (= 3 CP Microbiology of farming systems + 2 CP Geomatics); 1 CP Informatics. These sum to exactly 60. YEAR 2 — 60 ECTS: 6 CP Wildlife management in mountain areas (compulsory) + 24 CP Free choice courses + 30 CP Final Exam (thesis). WHERE THE THIRD SEMESTER FITS: the 24 CP of free choice is the vehicle for the exchange. Brochure: 'In the third semester, students can tailor their learning with optional courses that explore areas such as agricultural planning, specialised agronomy of mountain crops and advanced digitalisation. Students are encouraged to spend the third semester at one of the programme's partner universities, in particular the University of Applied Sciences Weihenstephan-Triesdorf in Bavaria, Germany. Activities include laboratory work, workshops, study trips and internships.' The fourth semester 'is devoted to the final thesis, an advanced research project that integrates the skills acquired.' NO OTHER VARIANTS: no dual-study/apprenticeship model, no double degree, no compulsory internship ('The internship is not compulsory'), and no evening or online delivery. english_only_accessibility: OPEN — this is one of the most accessible programmes at unibz for a candidate who speaks only English, and among the very easiest to actually get into. WHY IT IS OPEN: (1) the sole language requirement is English B2 — 'Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2' — with no German, no Italian, no third-language B1 threshold and no graduation language requirement of any kind; (2) all teaching is in English and the campus core is in Bolzano, an English-friendly university environment in an officially bilingual city; (3) the whole application is in English and requires no motivation letter, no video, no portfolio, no references and no interview; (4) the thesis is written and defended in English; (5) the academic entry gate is broad — four whole Italian bachelor classes (L-25, L-13, L-32, L-38) qualify outright, and the fallback route needs only 20 + 30 ECTS in L-25 sectors; (6) and, decisively, the competition is currently almost nonexistent: in 2026/27 Early Bird only 5 EU and 5 non-EU applicants were admitted against 25 and 10 places, and the lowest admitted non-EU score was 60/95 — an Italian-scale bachelor grade of about 23/30. THE HONEST QUALIFICATIONS. (i) THE THIRD SEMESTER. The programme's distinctive feature — a semester at Weihenstephan-Triesdorf — is at a German university of applied sciences where much master teaching is in German. An English-only student can still do the semester or stay in Bolzano, but will not get the full advertised experience without some German. (ii) THE 24 ECTS FREE-CHOICE BLOCK. unibz does not publish which free-choice courses are guaranteed in English each year; a small, new programme has a small elective menu. (iii) FIELD WORK AND INTERNSHIPS. South Tyrolean agriculture runs in German and Italian; farm visits, the named excursions (Kirnig - Südtiroler Edelpilze, Solos Farm) and voluntary internships with local businesses will often be conducted in German. (iv) THE REGIONAL JOB MARKET. Staying in South Tyrol after graduation as an agronomist or consultant realistically requires German; the degree itself does not. (v) DAILY LIFE AND ADMINISTRATION outside the university (housing, health service, municipal offices) is German/Italian. FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT SPECIFICALLY: a Ziraat Mühendisliği, Ziraat Fakültesi (tarla bitkileri, bahçe bitkileri, zootekni, toprak bilimi, bitki koruma, tarım ekonomisi, tarım makineleri), Biyoloji, Çevre Mühendisliği, Orman Mühendisliği, Su Ürünleri or Peyzaj Mimarlığı background is a strong fit and will normally clear the credit thresholds without difficulty. The realistic obstacles are administrative, not linguistic: (a) the CIMEA Statement of Comparability plus Statement of Verification required at enrolment (Türkiye is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so the ARDI Statement of Correspondence route applies plus CIMEA verification — see credential_recognition); (b) the single non-EU application window in March-April, with no second chance; (c) the €50 application fee and the visa/financial-means evidence; (d) proving B2 English — and, because a C1-level proof is worth 3 ranking points at no cost when your bachelor was English-medium, obtaining a medium-of-instruction letter from your university registrar is the single highest-return action available. BOTTOM LINE: rated 'open', not 'partially open'. The language architecture places no barrier at admission, during the taught programme, or at graduation. The German question is about maximising the experience and the local career, not about eligibility.
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato / limited places) decided by a purely DOCUMENT-BASED, FORMULA-DRIVEN ranking. There is NO entrance exam, NO TOLC, NO CENT-S, NO SAT, NO GRE or GMAT, NO portfolio, NO motivation letter, NO video, NO reference letters and NO INTERVIEW. Together with EMMA, this is one of the simplest admission procedures at unibz. THE TRIGGER CLAUSE, verbatim: 'If the number of eligible applicants exceeds the maximum number of available places (see section "Available places"), you will be assessed for admission based on your academic qualifications.' Note what this implies: the ranking is only a rationing device. In 2026/27 the number of eligible applicants was FAR BELOW the number of places in every session, so in practice every applicant who met the entry and language requirements and cleared the 55/95 floor was admitted. THE FOUR STEPS THAT ACTUALLY DECIDE YOUR CASE: (1) an ELIGIBILITY CHECK on the access qualification — either one of the four listed Italian bachelor classes (L-25, L-13, L-32, L-38) / a comparable foreign title, or the 20 + 30 ECTS fallback in L-25 sectors; (2) a LANGUAGE GATE at English B2, which is a hard knock-out — 'otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure' — and which was actually enforced in 2026/27 (applicant 157125 was excluded on this ground in the Late session); (3) an ARITHMETIC SCORE out of 95 derived from the bachelor grade, plus 2 for cum laude and plus 3 for a C1 English certificate; (4) a HARD THRESHOLD of 55/95, below which a candidate is excluded even if places remain empty. MANDATORY STRUCTURED UPLOAD: an Excel file — 'Excel file: Please use the file available in the application portal.' This is the study-career template in which you map your exams onto the L-25 credit sectors, and it is the instrument the Committee uses to verify the 20 + 30 ECTS thresholds. TIE-BREAK, in order, verbatim: 'If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet. In the event of further equal score, the younger applicant will be given priority (art. 3 L. 127/1997).' WHERE: the unibz Application Portal, https://aws.unibz.it/exup . An account plus a valid ID card or passport (front/back) is required before anything else, and 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. IRREVERSIBILITY: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' And twice over: 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' MULTIPLE APPLICATIONS ARE ALLOWED for EU/parity applicants: 'You might apply for more than one study programme. If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one.' Non-EU applicants living abroad get exactly one shot and, on Universitaly, may pre-enrol for one programme only.
academic_requirements:
THE ENTRY GRID IS BROAD AND UNUSUALLY EXPLICIT — four named Italian bachelor classes qualify outright, which is more generous than EMMA (which names only L-25). Verbatim from the admission-information PDF, the brochure and both signed ranking lists (identical wording): 'In order to gain admission to this programme without the need for further verification you need the following qualifications: • an adequate knowledge of the basic disciplines of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics and Biology and fundamental knowledge of the subjects preparatory to the fundamental disciplines of this degree class. • Bachelor graduates of the following Italian course categories (according to Ministerial Decree no. 270/04): – L-25 Agricultural, agri-food and forestry sciences and technologies – L-13 Biological sciences – L-32 Science and technology for the environment and nature – L-38 Zootechnical sciences and animal production technologies, as well as titles from the previous system that were equivalent to them, or a foreign title recognized as comparable. • In the presence of a three-year degree other than those listed above, candidates must have taken: – at least 20 ECTS of core subject areas (SSDs) among those listed in the Ministerial Decree of degree classes for class L-25, and – at least 30 ECTS of characterizing subject areas (SSDs) from among those listed in the Ministerial Decree of the degree classes for the L-25 category, relating to at least two subject areas. • For holders of a qualification obtained abroad, ECTS to SSDs will be allocated based on the evaluation of the contents of the courses followed in the student's previous career. • Any curricular integrations in terms of ECTS must be acquired prior to enrolment.'

HOW TO READ THIS AS A FOREIGN APPLICANT. There are effectively TWO ROUTES. ROUTE A — 'comparable foreign title': your degree is assessed as comparable to L-25, L-13, L-32 or L-38, and no credit counting is needed. In Turkish terms the obvious matches are Ziraat Mühendisliği / Ziraat Fakültesi programmes (→ L-25), Biyoloji and Moleküler Biyoloji ve Genetik (→ L-13), Çevre Mühendisliği, Çevre Bilimleri and Ekoloji (→ L-32), and Zootekni / Hayvansal Üretim and, arguably, Su Ürünleri (→ L-38). ROUTE B — the 20 + 30 credit fallback, used when your degree is something else (Gıda Mühendisliği, Orman Mühendisliği, Peyzaj Mimarlığı, Kimya, Coğrafya, Makine Mühendisliği with an agri-machinery emphasis, and so on). ROUTE B IS COMPARATIVELY LOOSE: only 50 ECTS in total (20 'attività di base' + 30 'attività caratterizzanti'), with the added diversity condition that the 30 must relate 'to at least two subject areas'. Compare the Master in Energy Engineering, which demands 85 ECTS across three separate blocks. Most four-year Turkish engineering or science degrees carry far more than 50 ECTS in these areas. THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT PRACTICAL DIFFERENCE FROM EMMA — A REMEDIAL WINDOW EXISTS AFTER ADMISSION IS DECIDED: 'Any curricular integrations in terms of ECTS must be acquired prior to enrolment.' EMMA's documents contain no such sentence. Here, a candidate who is a few credits short is not automatically dead: the missing credits must be in hand by the ENROLMENT deadline (13 October 2026 for the 2026/27 cycle), not by the application deadline. In principle these can be taken as single-subject/external-student courses at unibz or elsewhere. [uncertain] unibz does not spell out who authorises the integration, whether the Committee states the required credits in writing, or whether single-subject courses at unibz are guaranteed to be available in time. Anyone relying on this route must agree it in advance with the Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it) and the Degree Course Director. NO SSD CODE LIST IS PUBLISHED FOR THE ENTRY GRID. unibz points to 'the Ministerial Decree of degree classes for class L-25' rather than enumerating sectors. The reference frame is therefore the ministerial table for L-25, whose 'attività di base' are the mathematics/physics/informatics, chemistry and biology foundation areas and whose 'attività caratterizzanti' are the agronomic and crop-production, animal-production, agricultural-engineering and land-management, agricultural-economics and food/agri-industry areas. Since the 2024 Italian SSD reform these appear as codes of the AGRI-xx/x family (the teaching catalogue of this very programme uses AGRI-01/A, AGRI-02/A, AGRI-03/A, AGRI-04/B, AGRI-04/C, AGRI-05/A, AGRI-06/B, AGRI-08/A and AGRI-09/C), replacing the old AGR/01-AGR/20 codes; biology and chemistry foundations map to the BIOS-xx/x and CHEM-xx/x families, formerly BIO/xx and CHIM/xx. CONSEQUENCE: an applicant cannot self-certify eligibility from the published documents. Send an English transcript plus course descriptions to agriculture@unibz.it BEFORE the window opens. FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS: 'For holders of a qualification obtained abroad, ECTS to SSDs will be allocated based on the evaluation of the contents of the courses followed in the student's previous career', and 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' Prepare syllabi in English in advance. NOT YET GRADUATED: allowed. 'Applicants who do not yet have the required three-year degree may apply, but they must have the qualification by the enrolment deadline at the latest. Otherwise, they will be excluded from the procedure.' There is NO minimum-credits-so-far condition (no '≥120 ECTS' rule as in some unibz masters); the score then uses the 'weighted grade average expressed out of 30'. AT ENROLMENT the Diploma Supplement must show 'at least 180 credit points (ECTS)' and 'that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. MINIMUM GRADE: none is stated in words, but the 55/95 threshold is a de facto floor equivalent to roughly 22/30 on the Italian scale (see selection_scoring). DOUBLE ENROLMENT: maximum two simultaneous programmes, not in the same class, differing in at least two-thirds of content.
entry_exam_or_test: NO ENTRANCE EXAM OF ANY KIND. Specifically absent: no unibz admission test, no TOLC (TOLC-I / TOLC-E / TOLC-S / TOLC-B), no CENT-S, no SAT, no GRE, no GMAT, no subject test, no logical-reasoning test, no portfolio review, no video presentation and no oral interview. Admission is decided exclusively on uploaded documents plus the 95-point arithmetic score. The ranking lists confirm it: 'The evaluation is carried out exclusively on the basis of the documentation produced by the candidate with the pre-application.' THE ONLY EXAM AN APPLICANT MIGHT EVER SIT is the ENGLISH LANGUAGE PROFICIENCY EXAM at the unibz Language Centre, and only if they cannot prove B2 English by medium of instruction or by a recognised certificate. It is held ONLINE. 2026/27 SITTINGS AND REGISTRATION WINDOWS, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: EARLY BIRD — 'Language exams (online): 16/03/2026 (registration: 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration: 24/03 - 08/04/2026)'. LATE — 'Language exams (online): 22 - 26/06/2026 (registration: 28/05 - 15/06/2026)'. NOTE: unlike some sibling programmes, THIS programme's document lists NO language-exam sitting attached to the Additional Application Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026). An applicant using the additional window must therefore already hold acceptable proof of English; there is no unibz sitting in that period to fall back on. THE PROCEDURAL TRAP, verbatim: 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam.' In other words, opening your application does not register you for an exam, and the registration windows are shorter than the application windows. EVIDENCE THAT THE LANGUAGE GATE IS REAL: the signed Late Application ranking list contains a separate excluded-applicants table headed 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements for admission and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure', listing applicant 157125 — one of only four Late applicants. In a session with dozens of empty places, that candidate lost a place they would otherwise almost certainly have won, purely on paperwork. NO INTERVIEW EXISTS in any session — see the 'interview' field. WHERE TO REGISTER: in the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup), sections 'upload language certificates' and 'enrol for language exams', which only become available AFTER you have created an application under 'create/manage applications'.
selection_scoring:
A SINGLE ARITHMETIC FORMULA WITH THREE INPUTS. Verbatim (admission-information PDF, brochure and both signed ranking lists, identical): 'The Admission Committee can assign up to a max. of 95 points based on the: final bachelor grade expressed out of 30 (for applicants already graduated); weighted grade average expressed out of 30 (for applicants not graduated yet). The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude). Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points. Minimum score for admission is 55/95 points.'

THE INPUTS ARE THEREFORE: (1) the bachelor final grade, or the weighted average if you have not graduated, expressed out of 30 and mapped onto a base out of 95; (2) +2 for cum laude; (3) +3 for a C1-or-better English proof. NOTHING ELSE COUNTS — not your CV, not work experience, not publications, not internships, not Erasmus, not the reputation of your university, not a motivation letter, not an interview. This is one of the most mechanically predictable admissions at unibz: you can compute your own score before you apply. THE HEADLINE FIGURE IS MISLEADING IN ONE RESPECT: the stated maximum is '95 points', but the two bonuses sit on top of it, so the true ceiling is 100. The published Late Application list proves it — applicant 109370 scored exactly 100.00, which is only reachable as 95 (grade 30/30) + 3 (C1) + 2 (cum laude). DERIVED CONVERSION FORMULA — an INFERENCE, not a published rule, but it fits every one of the thirteen published 2026/27 scores. Base = 5 × (grade out of 30) − 55. That gives grade 22 → 55, 23 → 60, 24 → 65, 25 → 70, 26 → 75, 27 → 80, 28 → 85, 29 → 90, 30 → 95. Every observed score is either one of those bases or a base plus 3 (the C1 bonus) or, once, plus 3 and 2. Elegant confirmation: the published minimum of 55/95 maps exactly onto a bachelor grade of 22/30, the same 22/30 floor unibz states explicitly in its engineering masters, and the identical formula reproduces the score distribution of the sister programme EMMA. RULE OF THUMB: you need roughly a 22/30 Italian-scale weighted average to be eligible at all; a C1 English proof is worth about 0.6 of a grade point; cum laude is worth about 0.4. [uncertain] This mapping is reverse-engineered from published scores and is not stated by unibz anywhere; treat it as a strong working model, not an official rule, and note that the Committee may treat foreign grade scales with some judgement.

THE 2026/27 SCORE DATA IN FULL — this programme, unlike most at unibz, PUBLISHES INDIVIDUAL SCORES, and the picture is remarkable. EARLY BIRD (signed 22/05/2026), EU citizens and citizens enjoying parity of treatment, 5 admitted against 25 places: 98, 98, 93, 93, 73. EARLY BIRD, non-EU citizens living abroad, 5 admitted against 10 places: 93, 83, 83, 70, 60. LATE APPLICATION (signed 20/07/2026), EU only, 3 admitted: 100.00, 88.00, 65.00, with one further applicant (157125) excluded for failing the language requirement. There were NO waiting lists in either session — there was nothing to wait for. EFFECTIVE CUT-OFFS FOR 2026/27: none, in any session, beyond the statutory 55/95 floor. Every session was undersubscribed by a wide margin (5 of 25 EU places, 5 of 10 non-EU places, 3 more EU admits in a Late round that had at least 30 places available once unfilled Early Bird places rolled over). The lowest admitted score anywhere was 60 — an Italian-scale grade of about 23/30 with no English bonus. A REVEALING DETAIL: applicant 109370 appears in BOTH lists, at 98 in Early Bird and at 100.00 in Late. The only way to gain exactly 2 points between May and July is to have graduated cum laude in the interval — a neat live demonstration that the +2 is applied on top of a full 95 base, and that re-applying in a later session with an improved qualification is permitted and can raise your score. STRATEGIC READING. (1) Because the score is essentially the grade, an applicant with a modest GPA cannot compensate with experience — there is nowhere in the form to put it. (2) The C1 bonus is the only free lever, and it is decisive at the margin: in a normal, competitive year 3 points is roughly one full grade point of separation. (3) The tie-break rewards having already graduated, so applying in the cycle AFTER graduation is structurally safer than applying in your final undergraduate year. (4) MOST IMPORTANT: on current evidence this programme is not really a competition at all. For 2026/27 the binding constraints were eligibility, language proof and paperwork — not rank. Applicants should invest their effort in the credit-sector evidence and the language certificate, not in trying to out-score anyone.
bonus_points: EXACTLY TWO BONUSES EXIST, both small, both mechanical, and together worth 5 points. (1) C1 ENGLISH BONUS — 3 POINTS. Verbatim: 'Candidates who possess at least a C1 certificate in the official teaching language of the course (English) will be assigned 3 points.' CRUCIALLY THIS CAN BE EARNED WITHOUT SITTING ANY EXAM. unibz's own language-proof rules recognise as C1 both (a) 'the main teaching language in your final high school year, if English (recognised as C1)' and (b) 'a bachelor or master degree in English (recognised as C1)'. A candidate whose bachelor was 100% English-medium therefore gets the 3 points at zero cost, provided they upload 'a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies' when the degree certificate does not say so. This is the single highest-return, lowest-cost action available to an international applicant. Candidates from partly-English programmes (the common Turkish '30% İngilizce' model) cannot rely on this and should sit a certificate at C1 level: TOEFL iBT 95-113, IELTS Academic or General 7.0-8.0, Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE), C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) grade B/C, MET C1, or Aptis ESOL Advanced C1 (see certificate_rules). (2) CUM LAUDE ADJUSTMENT — 2 POINTS. Verbatim: 'The Admission Committee will assign 2 points to candidates who graduated with honors (cum laude).' Unlike in the sister programme EMMA, there is direct published evidence that this bonus is actually applied here: the Late Application list shows a score of 100.00, which is only reachable as 95 + 3 + 2. [uncertain] unibz does not say how a non-Italian distinction is mapped onto 'cum laude'. Whether a Turkish 'yüksek onur derecesi' / 'onur derecesi', a British first-class honours, a German 'mit Auszeichnung' or a US summa cum laude is accepted is left to the Committee, and there is no published equivalence table. If you hold such a distinction, state it explicitly in your uploaded documents and have the registrar describe it in English. WHAT DOES NOT EXIST HERE, in contrast to other unibz programmes: NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that is Software Engineering and Computing for Data Science, 3/2/1 points for a top-1000 / 1001-2000 / 2001-3000 university) — a degree from a highly ranked university is worth precisely nothing here; NO GMAT or GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance); NO startup-project presentation points (Entrepreneurship and Innovation, 30 points); NO video-presentation points (Energy Engineering, 10 points); NO CV or professional-experience points (Energy Engineering, 50 points); no points for research output, farm or field experience, agricultural extension work, or relevant employment. This is a grade-only competition with two small modifiers. PROPORTIONALITY CHECK: 5 bonus points on a 95-point base is about 5%, i.e. one full Italian grade point. In a year like 2026/27, where every eligible applicant was admitted, the bonuses changed nothing. In a future year where the programme becomes better known and the 35 EU places fill, they will be the difference between adjacent candidates — and the C1 proof will be the cheapest 3 points anyone can buy.
portfolio_and_materials: NO PORTFOLIO, NO MOTIVATION LETTER, NO VIDEO, NO REFERENCE LETTERS, NO RESEARCH PROPOSAL AND NOT EVEN A CV. Along with EMMA, this is the leanest application at unibz. Verbatim, the complete list: 'In the application portal, you must upload: 1. Qualification: ... 2. Excel file: Please use the file available in the application portal. 3. English language certifications (at least of level B2)' — plus the valid ID document required at account creation. Nothing is written, designed, filmed or argued; everything is obtained. (1) QUALIFICATION EVIDENCE, verbatim: 'if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or self-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded with the final grade and passed exams (if graduated) or, if not graduated yet, a certificate listing the exams passed; if graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with the passed exams (if graduated) or transcript of records (if not graduated yet) in Italian, German or English.' Mandatory contents: 'final grade, passed exams with indication of grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles). For qualifications obtained abroad, also: scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable).' THE GRADING-SCALE STATEMENT IS THE MOST COMMONLY OMITTED AND MOST DAMAGING OMISSION for a foreign applicant, because the ENTIRE ranking score is computed from your grade: if unibz cannot convert your grade it cannot score you. A Turkish applicant must supply an official statement of the scale (typically maximum 4.00, minimum 2.00 to graduate, plus the 100-point equivalence if the transcript uses one) — ideally the registrar's printed grading-system page of the transcript, not a self-written note. (2) THE EXCEL FILE — the structured study-career template downloaded from and re-uploaded to the Application Portal, in which you map your own exams onto the L-25 credit sectors so the Committee can verify the 20 + 30 ECTS thresholds. Fill it carefully and conservatively; it is the document on which your eligibility actually turns. [uncertain] This programme's text does not itself state a knock-out clause for a missing or incomplete Excel file, but it is listed as a mandatory upload and sibling unibz programmes state explicitly that applications without it are not considered. Treat it as mandatory and decisive. (3) ENGLISH LANGUAGE CERTIFICATION at B2 or above, or medium-of-instruction documentation, or registration for a unibz Language Centre exam. Administrative form, verbatim: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.' Certificates that cannot be uploaded 'can be sent by e-mail as PDF files or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline'. (4) ID: 'You need to create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport (front/back). Please note: if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure.' A blurred passport scan is an exclusion ground — check the upload after submitting. (5) FOREIGN QUALIFICATION HOLDERS must also upload the diploma: 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.' (6) PARITY-OF-TREATMENT APPLICANTS must upload a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno (or the renewal request if expired). Without it 'you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad'. STRONGLY ADVISED THOUGH NOT LISTED: English course syllabi / descriptions with contact hours, because 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' Having these ready shortens the assessment and reduces the risk of an unfavourable credit mapping. FORMAT LIMITS: unibz publishes NO file-size cap, page limit or word limit for this programme — there is no equivalent of the 20 MB portfolio PDF in the Design programmes or the 2-3 minute video in Energy Engineering, because there is no creative submission at all. HARD RULES: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.' And, stated twice: 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.'
interview: NO INTERVIEW — none, in any session, for any applicant category. The 2026/27 admission-information PDF, the 2026/27 brochure, the programme page and BOTH signed 2026/27 ranking-list decrees contain no reference to an interview, colloquium, videoconference, oral assessment, convocation or 'adequacy of personal preparation' hearing. The word does not appear. The Admission Committee — President Prof. Christian Fischer, members Prof. Andreas Gronauer and Dr. Thomas Zanon — decides on uploaded documents alone. The Early Bird ranking list states it flatly: 'The evaluation is carried out exclusively on the basis of the documentation produced by the candidate with the pre-application.' THIS IS A REAL ADVANTAGE OVER COMPARABLE PROGRAMMES. The Master in Energy Engineering runs a 'mandatory interview' for non-EU applicants and excludes those who 'did not participate'; several unibz masters convene threshold candidates (Computing for Data Science holds interview days). Here there is nothing to schedule, nothing to rehearse, no time-zone or connectivity risk, and no chance of a technical failure costing you a place. THE FLIP SIDE, and it matters: there is NO opportunity to explain a weak transcript, a career change, a non-obvious degree background or a difficult academic year. There is no human conversation anywhere in the process. Your grade, your credit mapping and your language proof ARE the application. If your case needs explanation, the only channel is a pre-application e-mail to the Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it) or the Degree Course Director — before you apply, not after. NO HISTORICAL INTERVIEW EITHER: because the programme has existed only since 2025/26, there is no earlier procedure in which an interview was used and later dropped (contrast EMMA, whose 2019/20 manifesto listed 'Academic qualification and eventual interview'). [uncertain] unibz can reinstate procedural elements from one cycle to the next, and this programme's procedure is only two cycles old and demonstrably still being tuned. Re-read the current-cycle admission-information PDF before applying in 2027/28 rather than relying on this record.
conditional_admission: YES — conditional (provisional) admission for not-yet-graduated applicants is explicitly available, and the rules are generous in one respect and unforgiving in another. THE CORE RULE, verbatim from the admission-information PDF: 'Applicants who do not yet have the required three-year degree may apply, but they must have the qualification by the enrolment deadline at the latest. Otherwise, they will be excluded from the procedure. Proof of possession of the qualification must be provided by the enrolment deadline.' The signed ranking lists add the operative wording: 'applicants who have not concluded their bachelor's degree are provisionally admitted: requirement for admission is the conclusion of the bachelor studies by the enrolment deadline (13 October 2026, 12 midday).' GENEROUS ASPECT — NO MINIMUM-CREDIT CONDITION. Unlike several unibz masters (≥120 ECTS already earned, or ≥140 for Data Analytics for Economics and Management), this programme imposes NO threshold of credits earned so far. Any enrolled bachelor student may apply; their score is then computed from the 'weighted grade average expressed out of 30' instead of a final grade. STRICT ASPECT — THE TIE-BREAK PENALISES YOU: 'If scores are equal, applicants who have already graduated take precedence over applicants who have not graduated yet.' In an oversubscribed round you lose every tie. In 2026/27 nothing was oversubscribed, so this bit nobody — but it will matter as the programme fills. DEADLINE FOR 2026/27: graduation must be completed and proven by 13 October 2026, 12:00 midday. THE SAFETY VALVE, and it is important to read it correctly, verbatim: 'Advice: If you achieve your qualification after the enrolment deadline, you should not pay the tuition fees to confirm the study place. You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there are study places still available, you can enrol by 11 December 2026.' The Early Bird ranking list repeats this with 'a late enrolment request to the Rector'. Two practical points: (a) if you know you will graduate in November, do NOT pay the €600 first instalment, because 'If by paying the 1st instalment you have confirmed the study place, there will be no refund of the tuition fees' except for non-EU applicants refused entry documents; (b) the late route is discretionary and depends on places remaining — which, in a programme running at roughly a quarter of capacity, is currently a very safe bet, but is not a right. NOTE a wording drift between documents: the Late Application list phrases it as 'you can enrol by 11 December 2026' without repeating the 'only if there are study places still available' proviso that the admission PDF and Early Bird list both carry; the restrictive version should be assumed to govern. A SECOND, SEPARATE RESERVATION applies to all foreign qualifications: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified', and 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded... If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' A THIRD applies to every non-EU citizen living abroad: 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' Your place therefore depends on a consular act you do not control — start the Universitaly and visa process the day the ranking list appears. A FOURTH, PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ONE: 'Any curricular integrations in terms of ECTS must be acquired prior to enrolment' — see academic_requirements. This is effectively a conditional admission on academic content, not just on graduation, and it is unusual and useful. FINAL WARNING, verbatim: 'If you have been admitted in the ranking list, but you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' [uncertain] The published 2026/27 lists carry the provisional-admission asterisk as a blanket footnote rather than marking individual applicants, so the number of conditionally admitted students in this cohort cannot be determined from the documents.
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE — no OFA, no additional learning requirements, no credit debts, no remedial obligations after enrolment. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, nor the brochure, nor either signed ranking list mentions OFA, 'obblighi formativi aggiuntivi' or any equivalent; the lists carry no OFA markers. WHY THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT APPLY: OFA is an Italian device reserved for FIRST-CYCLE, open-access programmes where a candidate fails a compulsory entrance test — at unibz it is used in the Bachelor in Economics and Management, the Bachelor in Economics, Politics and Ethics and the Bachelor in Tourism, Sport and Event Management, all tied to a mathematics test. This is a restricted-access SECOND-CYCLE programme with no entrance test at all, so there is nothing for an OFA to attach to. Italian law also does not permit master-level admission with curricular credit debts to be settled after enrolment: the L-25 credit thresholds must be satisfied BEFORE the student becomes a student. THE FUNCTIONAL EQUIVALENT SITS EARLIER, AND IT IS BETTER THAN AN OFA. This programme's admission text contains a sentence its sister programmes do not: 'Any curricular integrations in terms of ECTS must be acquired prior to enrolment.' A candidate who is short of the 20 'attività di base' or 30 'attività caratterizzanti' credits is not necessarily refused — the deficit must simply be closed before enrolment (13 October 2026 for the 2026/27 cycle), rather than before application. The natural vehicle is single-subject / external-student enrolment at unibz (https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/single-subject-courses) or equivalent courses elsewhere. [uncertain] unibz publishes no procedure for this: it does not say who determines the missing credits, whether the Committee issues a written integration requirement, how integrations taken at another institution are validated, or whether the relevant unibz single-subject courses are timetabled early enough to finish before 13 October. Because the sentence is unusually favourable and unusually vague, anyone intending to rely on it must agree it in writing with the Faculty Secretariat (agriculture@unibz.it) and the Degree Course Director (Prof. Christian Fischer) BEFORE applying. Do not assume a shortfall will be waved through. SEPARATELY, recognition of credits already earned is a post-enrolment matter and is not an OFA: 'Credit points from previous university studies can only be recognised after enrolment if the exams taken at the university of provenance are equivalent in content to those offered at unibz.'
language_requirements: ONE REQUIREMENT, AND ONLY ONE: ENGLISH AT B2 (CEFR) FOR ADMISSION. Verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.' There is NO German requirement, NO Italian requirement, NO third-language B1 threshold and NO exit/graduation language requirement anywhere in the governing documents. This is the lightest language profile unibz offers, shared with its other fully English-taught masters (EMMA, Energy Engineering, Software Engineering) and in sharp contrast to the trilingual programmes, which require C1/B2 at entry and C1/C1/B1 to graduate. THE GATE IS A HARD KNOCK-OUT AND IS ENFORCED. Failure to prove B2 means exclusion from the procedure regardless of your grade. The signed 2026/27 Late Application ranking list carries a dedicated exclusion table: 'The following persons do not meet the language requirements for admission and are therefore excluded from the admission procedure' — applicant 157125. That is one of only four Late applicants, in a session with dozens of empty places. The lesson is blunt: in this programme, more candidates are lost to language paperwork than to competition. B2 IS THE FLOOR, C1 IS THE TARGET. A C1-or-better proof adds 3 points to the ranking score, and unibz recognises an English-medium high-school final year or an English-medium bachelor/master degree AS C1 — so for many international applicants the 3 points cost nothing but a registrar's letter. HOW AND WHERE TO PROVE IT: in the Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup), sections 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', which become available only AFTER you create an application under 'create/manage applications'. Administrative form, verbatim: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.' Certificates that cannot be uploaded 'can be sent by e-mail as PDF files or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline'. A TIMING TRAP SPECIFIC TO THE 2026/27 ADDITIONAL SESSION (open 18/08 - 04/09/2026): no unibz Language Centre sitting is scheduled in that window, and the additional-session page warns that such applicants 'cannot attend the intensive language courses held in September'. Anyone applying in the additional window must already hold acceptable proof. NON-BINDING BUT REAL: German is the working language of South Tyrolean and Bavarian agriculture, of the encouraged HSWT third semester, and of much of daily life outside the university. unibz Language Centre courses in German and Italian are available voluntarily and carry no graduation consequence — but they are the difference between a degree and a career in this region.
entry_levels_by_position: ENGLISH B2 / no second language / no third language — in unibz's positional notation, B2 / none / none. unibz expresses language requirements by POSITION (first, second, third teaching language) rather than by named language, because in its trilingual programmes the same CEFR grid applies whichever of German, Italian and English a student places first. This programme has only ONE teaching language, English, in first position, required at B2 to gain admission. No level is required in a second or third language at any point, at entry or at graduation, because the programme is not trilingual. CALIBRATION ACROSS UNIBZ, so the figure can be read correctly: trilingual bachelors run B2/B2/none (Bachelor in Computer Science) or B2/B1/none (Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering); trilingual masters in the Faculty of Economics and Management run C1/B2/none (Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance, Master in Accounting and Finance); the English-taught masters — this one, EMMA, Energy Engineering, Software Engineering, Computing for Data Science — run B2/none/none. Against that spread, B2/none/none is the least demanding language profile available at unibz. THE ONE NUANCE UNIQUE TO THIS PROGRAMME: the encouraged third semester is at a GERMAN university of applied sciences (Weihenstephan-Triesdorf), so German has real practical weight in the second year even though it carries no formal level requirement and no position in the grid. Structurally this is the mirror image of EMMA, where the German-speaking second year is compulsory; here it is optional, which is why the programme is rated 'open' rather than 'partially open' for English-only candidates. NOTE ALSO WHAT THE POSITIONAL GRID DOES NOT CAPTURE: there is no exam-attendance language gate, no language course inside the study plan (the plan's 60 first-year credits are entirely disciplinary), and no language element in the thesis or final exam.
exit_levels: NO EXIT / GRADUATION LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT. Neither the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, nor the brochure, nor either signed ranking list states any exit level; the entire language section is headed 'Entry level (to gain admission)' and covers admission only. This places the programme firmly on the English-taught side of unibz's two-model system. The unibz Study Guide's C1/C1/B1 graduation model — under which a student 'will need to certify two languages at the C1 level and the third language at the B1 level' in order to graduate — applies to TRILINGUAL programmes. An entirely English-taught master 'does not include language requirements in other languages', with Language Centre courses offered as an optional extra. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT SOUNDS: the exit requirement is the single biggest hidden risk of studying at unibz. In the trilingual programmes, students routinely gain admission and then cannot graduate on time because they have not certified the second and third languages — a well-known source of delay. Here, once you are admitted with B2 English, no further language certification stands between you and the degree. The 30 ECTS thesis is written and defended in English. THERE IS ALSO NO INTERNAL LANGUAGE PROGRESSION ELEMENT: the 120-credit study plan contains no 'Scientific English' or academic-writing course (EMMA's 2019/20 plan once had a compulsory 3 CP 'Scientific English (C1-level)'; this plan has nothing of the kind). Every one of the first-year 60 credits is disciplinary. VOLUNTARY AND STRONGLY RECOMMENDED ANYWAY: German at the unibz Language Centre. It carries no graduation consequence, but it governs (a) how much of the HSWT Weihenstephan-Triesdorf third semester is usable, (b) how well internships and field work with South Tyrolean farms go, and (c) whether the South Tyrol / Tyrol / Bavaria agricultural job market is open to you after graduation. For a graduate intending to stay in the region, German is a career requirement even though it is not a degree requirement.
third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE — there is no second or third teaching language, therefore no third-language B1 threshold and no exam-attendance language gate of any kind. The rule this field exists to capture — a B1 level in the third language required from the second semester of the first year before a student may sit exams — belongs exclusively to unibz's TRILINGUAL programmes. It appears nowhere in this programme's 2026/27 admission-information PDF, brochure, programme page or ranking lists, and it cannot apply to a degree whose 'official teaching language is English' with no other language named. There is likewise no first-language or second-language threshold gating exam attendance at any point across the four semesters, no language checkpoint before the thesis, and no language condition attached to the free-choice credits or to the final exam. The only language condition attached to this programme is the B2 English entry gate, which is settled before admission and never revisited. THE STUDY-GUIDE PAGE THAT GOVERNS THIS PROGRAMME is 'English-taught master programmes', not 'Trilingual master programmes'. The admission PDF does carry a generic pointer — 'For information on studying in three languages also visit the following page' — but that is unibz boilerplate present on every programme's document and creates no obligation here. NOR DOES THE EXCHANGE CREATE ONE: the encouraged third semester at Weihenstephan-Triesdorf imposes no CEFR requirement from the unibz side, because it is optional mobility rather than a structural part of the degree. [uncertain] Whether HSWT itself sets a German or English level for incoming exchange students in particular modules is not published by unibz and should be checked with the International Relations Office if you intend to take the exchange.
proof_pathways:
FOUR ACCEPTED WAYS TO PROVE ENGLISH, listed verbatim in the admission-information PDF. Two of them require no exam at all and, better still, count as C1 — which also earns the 3 ranking-score bonus points.

PATHWAY 1 — MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT SCHOOL: 'the main teaching language in your final high school year, if English (recognised as C1). Foreign qualifications: If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction.' Relevant to graduates of English-medium high schools (in Türkiye, an Anadolu/private lisesi teaching wholly in English, or an international/IB school).

PATHWAY 2 — MEDIUM OF INSTRUCTION AT UNIVERSITY: 'a bachelor or master degree in English (recognised as C1). unibz graduates must upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they have passed language exams at the unibz Language Centre (B2, B2+ or C1). THIS IS THE HIGHEST-VALUE PATHWAY FOR MOST INTERNATIONAL APPLICANTS: it costs one registrar's letter, satisfies the B2 requirement, and is recognised as C1, so it also delivers the +3 bonus. certificate_rules:
GOVERNED BY THE 'Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants', RESOLUTION OF THE UNIVERSITY COUNCIL No. 16/2026 (published trilingually as Beschluss des Universitätsrates Nr. 16/2026 / Delibera del Consiglio dell'Università n. 16/2026), at https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf . The rules are strict, mechanical and unforgiving, and they cause more avoidable exclusions than any other part of the application.

THE SIX RULES THAT MATTER, verbatim from the English section:
(1) FOUR SKILLS, ONE ISSUER: a certificate must 'include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself'. 'Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted.'
(2) THE LOWEST SUB-SKILL DECIDES: 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed.' An IELTS report with three 7.0s and a 6.0 in writing is a B2, not a C1.
(3) NO COMPENSATION, NO AVERAGING: 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.'
(4) FIVE-YEAR VALIDITY, counted generously by calendar year: international certificates must have been obtained within the last five years before submission, and the whole calendar year counts from 1 January ('Es gilt das gesamte Kalenderjahr ab dem 1. Januar' / 'sono validi i certificati rilasciati a partire dal 1° gennaio del quinto anno precedente alla presentazione'). Items in the 'Further proofs / Ulteriori attestati / Weitere Nachweise' section — unibz Language Centre internal exams, the Autonome Provinz Bozen bilingualism certificate (Zweisprachigkeitsnachweis) and similar — have UNLIMITED validity.
(5) HOME-EDITION AND ONLINE EXAMS ARE NOT RECOGNISED, with named exceptions: 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list.' In the English table, TOEFL, TOEIC, IELTS and Aptis carry the asterisk meaning 'Also accepted as home edition'. Everything else must have been sat in person.
(6) WHAT IS NEVER ACCEPTED: course attendance certificates, end-of-course tests, exams from private language schools, placement-test results, and certificates issued by individual teachers or lecturers. And explicitly: 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.'

THE ENGLISH SCORE BANDS THAT MATTER FOR THIS PROGRAMME (B2 = admission floor; C1 = admission plus 3 bonus points):
B2 — TOEFL iBT 72-94; IELTS (Academic and General) 5.5-6.5; Cambridge B2 First (FCE) grade B or C, B2 First for Schools grade B or C, B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage) grade B or C, B1 Preliminary (PET) grade A, B1 Preliminary for Schools grade A, B1 Business Preliminary (BEC Preliminary) pass with distinction, C1 Advanced (CAE) at level B2, C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) at level B2; TOEIC Listening 400+, Reading 385+, Speaking 160+, Writing 150+; Michigan MET B2 (all 4 skills), ECCE; Aptis ESOL General B2, Aptis ESOL Advanced B2.
C1 — TOEFL iBT 95-113; IELTS (Academic and General) 7.0-8.0; Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) grade B or C, B2 First (FCE) grade A, B2 First for Schools grade A, B2 Business Vantage (BEC Vantage) grade A, C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) grade B or C, C2 Proficiency (CPE) at level C1; TOEIC Listening 490+, Reading 455+, Speaking 180+, Writing 180+; Michigan MET C1 (all 4 skills); Aptis ESOL Advanced C1.
C2 (also earns the bonus, since the rule says 'at least a C1 certificate') — TOEFL iBT 114-120; IELTS 8.5+; Cambridge C1 Advanced (CAE) grade A, C1 Business Higher (BEC Higher) grade A, C2 Proficiency (CPE) grade A/B/C; Michigan ECPE; Aptis ESOL Advanced C2.

PRACTICAL ADVICE FOR A TURKISH APPLICANT: the widely used Turkish national exam YDS/e-YDS is NOT in unibz's recognised list, and neither are university-internal proficiency exams (hazırlık atlama sınavı) or private-school certificates. Plan for IELTS Academic (home edition accepted) or TOEFL iBT (home edition accepted), and aim for 7.0 / 95 rather than the 5.5 / 72 minimum, because the extra band is worth 3 ranking points. Above all, check the LOWEST sub-score: rule (2) is what most often demotes an intended C1 to a B2.

The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' THE ONE-PROGRAMME LIMIT ON UNIVERSITALY IS THE HARD STRATEGIC CONSTRAINT: you may pay to secure up to two unibz places, but you can only pre-enrol for one on Universitaly, and it is that single choice the consulate acts on. REFUND EXCEPTION, unique to this group: fees paid are not refundable 'except for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country'. THE €50 APPLICATION FEE is non-refundable and is charged regardless of outcome. THE PARITY-OF-TREATMENT ESCAPE HATCH: a non-EU citizen who already holds a valid Italian residence permit for work, family, political or humanitarian asylum, or religious reasons is treated as an EU citizen and gains access to all three windows and to the EU quota — see parity_of_treatment. A study or tourism permit does NOT qualify.
parity_of_treatment: unibz splits applicants into three categories, not two, and the third — 'citizens given parity of treatment' — is decisive for many international candidates because it converts a single April deadline into three application windows and moves you from the 10-place non-EU quota into the 35-place EU quota. THE DEFINITION, verbatim: 'Considered as equivalent are: 1. Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; 2. Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request. Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' THE FOUR QUALIFYING PERMIT GROUNDS ARE THEREFORE: work (lavoro subordinato or autonomo), family reasons (ricongiungimento familiare / motivi familiari, including the permit held by the spouse or child of a resident), political or humanitarian asylum (including subsidiary protection), and religious reasons. A long-term EU residence permit (permesso di soggiorno UE per soggiornanti di lungo periodo) also falls in this space. EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED: a study permit (permesso per motivi di studio) and a tourist visa. This is the trap that catches people most often — a student already in Italy on a study permit for a bachelor is NOT a parity applicant and must still compete in the non-EU quota with the April-only deadline. WHY IT MATTERS SO MUCH HERE, in concrete 2026/27 numbers: as a parity applicant you get Early Bird (25 places) + Late (10 places, plus everything unfilled from Early Bird) + the Additional Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026, still open on 2026-08-29), you pay NO €50 application fee, you skip the Universitaly pre-enrolment, you skip the visa entirely, and you may apply to more than one unibz programme. As a non-EU applicant abroad you get one April window, 10 places, a €50 fee, a mandatory Universitaly single-programme pre-enrolment, a consular visa process, and a place that stays provisional 'until the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz'. THE PROCEDURAL RULE IS UNFORGIVING AND WORTH REPEATING: parity status is not automatic from your declared residence — it depends entirely on uploading the permit copy into the Application Portal. Fail to upload it and 'you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad'. The ranking list adds the same warning from the other side: 'If you have declared to be resident in Italy but have not attached to your application a copy of your valid residence permit for Italy... you are ranked together with the non-EU citizen resident abroad.' FOR TURKISH APPLICANTS: Türkiye is NOT in the parity list, so a candidate applying from Türkiye is a non-EU citizen living abroad. Parity applies only to Turkish citizens ALREADY resident in Italy on a qualifying (non-study) permit — for example someone on a work permit in Bolzano, Trento, Verona or Milan, or a family-reunification permit. There is also a separate scholarship consequence: the provincial study grant requires either a long-term residence permit or one full uninterrupted year of residence in South Tyrol (see scholarships_grants).

The Additional Session then draws on whatever is still unfilled; unibz publishes no separate quota for it.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED IN 2026/27 — AND IT IS STRIKING. Early Bird (signed 22/05/2026): 5 EU/parity applicants admitted against 25 places (20% fill), scores 98, 98, 93, 93, 73; and 5 non-EU applicants admitted against 10 places (50% fill), scores 93, 83, 83, 70, 60. HOW TO READ THIS. The programme is in its SECOND intake and is not yet known to international applicants: it has no Italian or German page, no alumni, no rankings presence and almost no third-party visibility. The result is one of the least competitive genuinely English-taught masters in Italy right now — 5 admitted non-EU students in a normal year, from a pool small enough that the bottom admitted score (60/95, about 23/30) sat well below what any competitive programme would take.

THE CAVEAT, and it should be taken seriously: THIS WILL NOT LAST. Low numbers in a new programme are a transient artefact of low visibility, not a structural feature. As soon as the programme appears in aggregator databases, gets translated pages, and produces its first graduates, the 10 non-EU places will become genuinely contested — at which point the 55/95 floor stops being the binding constraint and the score distribution starts to matter. An applicant reading this in 2027 should not assume 2026/27's numbers repeat.
