THE APPLICATION ITSELF NEEDS FOUR THINGS. THE ENROLMENT NEEDS FIVE MORE. Keeping the two stages apart is the key to not losing a place.

AT APPLICATION (Application Portal, https://aws.unibz.it/exup):
(0) ACCOUNT + ID — 'You need to create an account and upload a valid ID card or passport (front/back). Please note: if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure.'
(1) QUALIFICATION — 'if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or self-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded with the final grade and passed exams (if graduated) or, if not graduated yet, a certificate listing the exams passed; if graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with the passed exams (if graduated) or transcript of records (if not graduated yet) in Italian, German or English.' It must contain 'final grade, passed exams with indication of grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles)' and, for foreign qualifications, 'scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable)'. THE GRADING SCALE IS NOT OPTIONAL — the whole ranking score is computed from your grade.
(2) THE EXCEL FILE — 'Excel file: Please use the file available in the application portal.' The structured study-career template in which you map your exams onto the L-25 credit sectors. This is the document the Committee uses to check the 20 + 30 ECTS thresholds.
(3) ENGLISH LANGUAGE CERTIFICATION — 'English language certifications (at least of level B2)', or medium-of-instruction evidence, or registration for a unibz Language Centre exam.
(4) IF YOUR QUALIFICATION IS FOREIGN, also the diploma: 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.'
(5) IF YOU CLAIM PARITY OF TREATMENT, a copy of the valid Italian permesso di soggiorno (or the renewal request if expired). Omit it and you are reclassified as a non-EU applicant abroad.
NOT REQUIRED, and worth stating because applicants waste time on them: no CV, no motivation letter, no reference letters, no research proposal, no portfolio, no video.
ADVISABLE THOUGH NOT LISTED: English syllabi / course descriptions with contact hours, since 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.'

AT ENROLMENT, IF YOU HAVE A FOREIGN UNIVERSITY DEGREE — this is where most of the real work sits, and it must be done between the ranking list and 13 October:
• 'degree diploma of your Bachelor';
• 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)';
• 'Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme';
• plus, depending on the country: for EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein — the ARDI Statement of Correspondence; for non-EU signatories of the Lisbon Convention — the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification; for non-EU non-signatories — the CIMEA Statement of Comparability AND the CIMEA Statement of Verification.
'unibz performs the necessary checks on your foreign qualification and in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents.' 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded.'

FOR STUDENTS TRANSFERRING FROM ANOTHER ITALIAN UNIVERSITY: 'a copy of the transfer application presented at the university of provenance', to be submitted to the Student Office at the beginning of the academic year.

FOR NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD, additionally: the Universitaly pre-enrolment (mandatory, one programme only), the consular study visa, and — after arrival — the residence-permit application within 8 working days, with the permesso di soggiorno then handed in to the Student Office.

TWO RULES THAT END APPLICATIONS: 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified' and 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.'

[uncertain] The Excel template is only visible inside the Application Portal after an application is created, so its exact columns and the level of detail expected cannot be described from public sources. Create the application early in the window, download the file, and if the mapping of your exams to L-25 sectors is not obvious, ask agriculture@unibz.it before submitting — the form cannot be corrected after sending.
application_fee: €50, charged to ONE GROUP ONLY: non-EU citizens living outside Italy. Verbatim, under the heading 'Non-EU-Citizens (living outside of Italy)': 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore. Application fee: € 50.' NOT CHARGED to EU citizens, to citizens given parity of treatment (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino, Vatican City, and non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian residence permit for work, family, asylum or religious reasons), or to applicants already resident in Italy on a qualifying permit. For those groups the application is free in all three sessions. NON-REFUNDABLE, and independent of outcome: it is paid to have the application assessed, not to hold a place. It is separate from, and additional to, the €600 first tuition instalment that secures an admitted place. IT IS NOT THE MAIN COST OF APPLYING FROM OUTSIDE THE EU. Budget realistically for the surrounding documentation: the CIMEA Statement of Comparability and Statement of Verification (each carries a CIMEA fee and takes weeks), certified translations where the documents are not in Italian, German or English, an IELTS or TOEFL sitting if you cannot prove medium of instruction, consular visa fees, and courier costs. For a Turkish applicant the CIMEA and language-test costs together will typically exceed the €50 fee by a large multiple. PRACTICAL NOTE: because there is exactly one non-EU window per year, the €50 buys one attempt per academic year. Do not spend it on an application whose credit-sector evidence has not first been checked with the Faculty Secretariat. [uncertain] unibz does not publish the accepted payment methods for the application fee, whether it is waived for any category (for example holders of Italian government scholarships), or whether it is charged again if an applicant re-applies in a subsequent year. The admission-information PDF states only the amount and the group.
tuition_or_fees_link: APPROXIMATELY €1,200 PER YEAR — one of the lowest tuition levels of any public university in Western Europe, and the same for EU and non-EU students alike (unibz does NOT charge differentiated international fees). Brochure 'At a Glance': 'Tuition fees: ca. € 1200 per year'. Admission-information PDF, verbatim: 'Fees amount to € 1200. 1st instalment (€ 600): includes the revenue stamp of € 16. 2nd instalment (€ 600): must be paid by March of the following year.' FEES PAGE: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees (unibz Study Guide). For 2026/27 it gives the operative dates and the out-of-time surcharge: 1st instalment €600 by 13 October 2026 and 2nd instalment €600 by 31 March 2027 for students within one year of the normal programme length; for students from the second year beyond the normal length the 1st instalment rises to €900 (2nd instalment unchanged at €600). A €16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) applies to everyone, including those exempt from the fees themselves. THE FIRST INSTALMENT DOES DOUBLE DUTY: paying it is also the act that SECURES YOUR ADMITTED PLACE, and it falls much earlier than 13 October — by 05/06/2026 for Early Bird admits, 06/08/2026 for Late admits, 25/09/2026 for Additional Session admits. Miss it and 'you will automatically be excluded and the next applicant in the ranking list will be admitted'. LATE PAYMENT: 'Delayed payment of the second instalment will result in a fine being levied' — the Study Guide quantifies it at €30 — and the account is blocked: 'If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes.' NO REFUNDS: 'If you drop out of a programme, interrupt your studies or are excluded from studies, you are not entitled to reimbursement of the fees.' The one exception is a non-EU applicant living abroad who fails to obtain the entry documents from the Italian authorities. EXEMPTIONS, verbatim: 'Students with a disability recognized under article 3, paragraph 1, of Law No 104/1992, or with a disability up to or exceeding 66%: the disability certificate, issued by the health authorities, must be handed in at the beginning of the academic year' and 'Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government.' Both still pay the €16 stamp. Separately: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.' WHAT €1,200 DOES NOT COVER, and this is the number that actually decides affordability: unibz tells non-EU applicants to budget 'at least € 800 per month' for living costs in Bozen-Bolzano, i.e. roughly €9,600 a year, plus health insurance and visa costs. Two years therefore cost about €2,400 in tuition against roughly €19,000-24,000 in living costs. See non_eu_visa_process for the figures the consulate applies. [uncertain] The €1,200 figure is written as 'ca.' (approximately) and unibz reserves the right to change it; the fees page is the authoritative source for the cycle you actually enrol in. It is also not stated whether the part-time route (chosen in October after enrolment) attracts a reduced fee — a plausible saving that should be checked with the Student Office before opting in.
scholarships_grants:
THERE IS NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC SCHOLARSHIP. No faculty scholarship, no HSWT mobility grant, no industry-sponsored place and no merit award attached to this master is published anywhere on the programme page, in the brochure or in the admission-information PDF. Funding comes from three general channels, and the first is by far the most important.

(1) THE ORDINARY PROVINCIAL STUDY GRANT (borsa di studio universitaria, Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano) — the big one. For 2026/27 the amounts run 'da euro 305,00 fino al massimo di euro 8.280,00' (€305 to a maximum of €8,280), paid in a single instalment, with the amount determined by the family's economic situation against the provincial VSE threshold table. Application window: 22/09/2026 to 03/11/2026, 12:00. Winning it also triggers a tuition refund: 'Students who benefit from a scholarship granted by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to receive a refund of the tuition fees.'
THE RESIDENCE BARRIER IS THE DECISIVE POINT FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS, verbatim from unibz: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption.' The provincial rules add that holders of a non-long-term permit must show uninterrupted South Tyrol residence for at least a year and present the original permit to the provincial office by the deadline (3 November 2026, 12:00). CONSEQUENCE: a newly arrived non-EU student CANNOT get this grant in their first year. They can apply from the second year. Merit conditions also apply from the second year onwards (for example at least 25 ECTS by the second year for full-time students, and at least 10 ECTS in the reference period 1 November - 31 October).

(2) THE PROVINCIAL MERIT SCHOLARSHIP (borse di studio per merito) — smaller, competitive, and effectively closed to first-year non-EU arrivals. In the most recent published call: 182 scholarships of €1,392.00 each; minimum grade average 28/30 (or a final thesis grade of at least 107/110; for foreign universities, 1.3 on the Austrian scale or equivalent); at least 42 ECTS earned in the reference period (1 November 2024 - 31 October 2025); enrolment must not exceed the normal course duration by more than six months; EU citizenship or equivalent residency status is required. Application window 16 March - 24 April 2026, 12:00. Note the 28/30 bar is high — on the conversion implied by this programme's own scoring formula, that is a base admission score of 85.

(3) OTHER CHANNELS listed by unibz: Italian government scholarships for foreign students (which also bring full tuition exemption at unibz — 'Foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government' are exempt, paying only the €16 stamp), Austrian and German national schemes, and DAAD programmes. Note the asymmetry: a DAAD SCHOLARSHIP is a funding route, but a DAAD LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE is explicitly not recognised for admission. unibz also lists a Municipality of Merano scholarship, but that is tied to Food and Enogastronomy Sciences, not to this programme. Erasmus+ mobility grants are the natural funding route for the third semester at Weihenstephan-Triesdorf, though unibz does not publish the arrangement for this programme.
Applications for provincial grants go through the South Tyrolean e-government service (civis.bz.it / mycivis.civis.bz.it); the South Tyrolean Students Association (sh.asus) assists with the forms. unibz's own page: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants .

REALISTIC FINANCIAL PICTURE FOR A NON-EU STUDENT: year 1 is self-funded — €1,200 tuition plus roughly €9,600 living costs, with no provincial grant available. From year 2, if you have been continuously resident in South Tyrol, the ordinary grant becomes reachable and can cover a large share of living costs while also refunding tuition. Budget for the full two years up front (the consulate will require it anyway: 'at least € 36,000' for a bachelor, '€ 24,000' for a master) and treat any grant as an improvement, not a plan.

[uncertain] Grant amounts, VSE thresholds and windows are set annually by provincial decree and the figures above are from the calls current on 2026-08-29; the €305-€8,280 range and the 182 × €1,392 merit call must be re-checked for the year you enrol. It is also not published whether students on the part-time route remain eligible for the ordinary grant on the same credit thresholds.
credential_recognition:
THE RECOGNITION ROUTE IS DECIDED BY YOUR COUNTRY'S RELATIONSHIP TO THE LISBON RECOGNITION CONVENTION, and unibz sets out three cases, verbatim:
'a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein: Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database – Italy.'
'b) Non-EU countries that are signatories to the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database – Italy and Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA).'
'c) Non-EU countries that are not signatories of the Lisbon Convention: Statement of Comparability of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA) and Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA).'

FOR TURKISH APPLICANTS: Türkiye IS a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so case (b) applies — the ARDI Statement of Correspondence PLUS the CIMEA Statement of Verification. The CIMEA Verification is the step most people underestimate: it is a genuine authenticity check in which CIMEA contacts the issuing university, and it can take several weeks. Start it as soon as the ranking list is published, not after arrival. [uncertain] unibz gives no processing-time guidance and does not say whether it will accept a CIMEA receipt or pending-application evidence at the enrolment deadline; ask the Student Office before 13 October if your CIMEA file is still open.

ALWAYS REQUIRED IN ADDITION, whichever case applies: the degree diploma; an 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)'; and the Diploma Supplement, 'where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. A Turkish transcript in Turkish must therefore be either issued in English by the registrar (the usual and cheaper route) or translated into Italian by a sworn translator.

THE 180-ECTS / 'GIVES ACCESS TO A MASTER' STATEMENT IS THE COMMONEST FAILURE POINT for four-year non-European bachelors. Turkish lisans degrees are typically four years and 240 ECTS, comfortably above 180, but many Turkish diploma supplements do not state ECTS at all or do not say the degree gives access to a second cycle. Ask the registrar to issue a Diploma Supplement in the EU format that makes both statements explicitly.

A SECOND, EARLIER AND DIFFERENT ASSESSMENT ALSO HAPPENS, and should not be confused with recognition: at APPLICATION the Admission Committee maps your exams onto the L-25 credit sectors ('For holders of a qualification obtained abroad, ECTS to SSDs will be allocated based on the evaluation of the contents of the courses followed in the student's previous career'), using your transcript and the Excel study-career file, and may request 'a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours'. CIMEA/ARDI documents are NOT required at that stage — they are enrolment documents.

STATUS UNTIL IT CLEARS: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified' and 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded... If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' The final backstop: 'Please note that if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'

unibz also runs a general 'Recognition of Foreign Qualifications' service, linked from the faculty navigation, and the Advisory Service (+39 0471 012100, apply@unibz.it) handles pre-application questions.
non_eu_visa_process:
A FIVE-STAGE CHAIN, and every stage has a hard gate. The unibz guidance for degree-seeking non-EU citizens living abroad is the governing source.

STAGE 1 — APPLY, ONCE. Early Bird only, 02/03 - 28/04/2026 noon for the 2026/27 cycle, €50 non-refundable fee. There is no second window.

STAGE 2 — SECURE THE PLACE. After the ranking list (by 27/05/2026; the signed list was dated 22/05/2026), pay the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon. Verbatim: 'Once the ranking list has been published, if you have gained admission, secure it by paying the first instalment and then start your visa application on the Universitaly portal.'

STAGE 3 — UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT, MANDATORY AND SINGLE-CHOICE. 'The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' The ranking list is blunter: 'Should you not follow this procedure, your direct online application to unibz will be declared null and void.' Portal: https://www.universitaly.it/ . You may pay to hold up to two unibz places, but you may pre-enrol for only one — so the Universitaly choice is the real decision.

STAGE 4 — THE CONSULAR STUDY VISA (visto per studio / type D). Applied for at the Italian Embassy or Consulate with jurisdiction over your residence. unibz is explicit that admission does not guarantee it: 'Please note that preliminary admission by unibz does not guarantee obtaining a visa, the issuing of which is the exclusive responsibility of embassies and consulates. Likewise, obtaining a visa for study purposes does not confer any right to perfecting the enrolment in a study programme.' The consulate then sends an official communication directly to unibz; until it arrives, 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted'.
PROOF OF FINANCIAL MEANS — THE FIGURES THE CONSULATE APPLIES, as published by unibz: living costs 'at least € 800 per month' excluding tuition, covering accommodation, food, study materials, leisure and clothing in the Bozen-Bolzano area, plus health insurance and visa expenses. Total estimated cost of studies: 'at least € 36,000' for a bachelor and '€ 24,000' for a master. For THIS two-year master, therefore, plan to evidence roughly €24,000 in addition to the €2,400 of tuition. Health insurance is required both for the visa and for the residence permit.

STAGE 5 — ARRIVAL, RESIDENCE PERMIT, ENROLMENT. 'According to Italian law, within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, you must have applied for the residence permit: as soon as you arrive, get in touch with the Advisory Service and you will be given the necessary information for starting the procedure.' The application kit requires the passport with valid entry visa, medical insurance and a housing contract or a declaration signed by the owner — so accommodation must be arranged before or immediately on arrival. 'Once you obtain your residence permit (permesso di soggiorno), you have to hand it in at the Student Office personally or via e-mail.' Online enrolment must be completed by 13/10/2026 noon.

WORKING WHILE STUDYING: students may work 'part-time for no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year'. At South Tyrolean wage levels that can cover a meaningful share of the €800/month, but it cannot be presented to the consulate as your means of subsistence.

THE ONE REFUND YOU ARE ENTITLED TO: fees are not refundable except 'for non-EU applicants living abroad who do not obtain the necessary documents for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country'. If the visa is refused, the €600 comes back; the €50 application fee does not.

IMPORTANT ONWARD CONSEQUENCE, SPECIFIC TO THIS PROGRAMME: the encouraged THIRD SEMESTER AT WEIHENSTEPHAN-TRIESDORF is in GERMANY. A non-EU student holding an Italian permesso di soggiorno for study may travel and study in another Schengen state for a limited mobility period under EU Directive 2016/801, but the German mobility notification and the interaction with an Italian permit renewal are real administrative work that must be started months ahead. [uncertain] Neither unibz nor the programme documents address the immigration mechanics of the HSWT semester for non-EU students at all. Anyone planning it should raise it with the unibz Advisory Service and the International Relations Office in the first weeks of year 1.

A SECOND CONSEQUENCE: the provincial study grant is closed to newly arrived non-EU students (long-term permit, or one uninterrupted year of South Tyrol residence, required), so year 1 must be fully self-funded — see scholarships_grants.

WHAT IS SOLID. Every date, quota, requirement, score, fee and rule in this record comes from unibz's own 2026/27 documents, all downloaded and text-extracted on 2026-08-29: the admission-information PDF and brochure (both stamped 'Latest update: 26.08.2026'), both signed ranking-list decrees, the programme page, the study-plan and course-offering pages, the additional-application-session page, the University Council Resolution 16/2026 certificate list, and the unibz Study Guide fees and study-grants pages. Where a figure comes from a provincial or third-party source it is attributed as such.

WHAT IS INFERRED RATHER THAN STATED.
(1) FIRST INTAKE 2025/26. unibz never says the programme is new. The conclusion rests on six convergent signals: no Wayback Machine capture of the programme page before 14/02/2025; a course-offering year selector that begins at 2025/26; HTTP 404 on the grade-statistics-lm-69 page while EMMA's equivalent returns 200; no Italian or German page; a 2026/27 catalogue containing all eleven year-1 courses but only one year-2 course; and a course renamed between the two cohorts. Each is weak alone; together they are strong. Still an inference.
(2) THE GRADE-TO-SCORE CONVERSION base = 5 × grade − 55. Fits all thirteen published 2026/27 scores and reproduces EMMA's distribution, but is nowhere published by unibz, and how foreign grading scales are normalised into 'out of 30' is not disclosed at all.
(3) THE TRUE MAXIMUM SCORE IS 100, NOT 95. Deduced from the published 100.00, which is only reachable as 95 + 3 + 2. unibz's text says 'up to a max. of 95 points' and never reconciles this.

OPEN QUESTIONS THAT MATTER TO AN APPLICANT, none of which unibz answers publicly.
(a) THE THIRD SEMESTER AT WEIHENSTEPHAN-TRIESDORF: no published information on the legal instrument (Erasmus+ vs bilateral), the number of exchange places, the selection procedure or internal deadline, the grant, which HSWT modules are available in English, or how a non-EU student's Italian residence permit interacts with a semester in Germany. Since this is the programme's headline feature, the gap is significant.
(b) THE 24 ECTS FREE-CHOICE BLOCK in year 2: no published catalogue, no statement of which courses are guaranteed in English, no indication of whether choices are drawn from the whole unibz offering or a faculty list.
(c) THE 'CURRICULAR INTEGRATIONS ... PRIOR TO ENROLMENT' CLAUSE: unusually favourable and completely unprocedural — who determines the shortfall, whether it is communicated in writing, whether courses taken elsewhere count, and whether unibz single-subject courses can realistically be completed before 13 October are all unstated.
(d) NO SSD LIST for the entry grid, so applicants cannot self-verify the 20 + 30 ECTS thresholds; the only route is to e-mail agriculture@unibz.it in advance.
(e) CUM LAUDE EQUIVALENCE for non-Italian distinctions is undefined.
(f) THE EXCEL STUDY-CAREER FILE is only visible inside the Application Portal, so its structure could not be described.

INTERNAL CONTRADICTIONS FOUND IN UNIBZ'S OWN DOCUMENTS.
(i) The double-enrolment example in this programme's documents reads 'LM-73 and LM-73' and, in one paragraph of the Early Bird list, 'LM-18/LM-18' — neither is this programme's class (LM-69). Boilerplate carried over from sibling documents.
(ii) The brochure study plan lists 'Farm management and entrepreneurship' (6 CP) where the live 2026/27 catalogue shows 'Agribusiness Management' (6 CP, code 47312). Almost certainly a rename, never announced.
(iii) The web study-plan widget renders 'Mountain crop ecosystems' as 6 CP and 'Rural and agricultural development' as 6 CP, giving a year-1 total of 59; the brochure's 3 CP and 9 CP give exactly 60. The brochure is treated as authoritative here.
(iv) The programme page does NOT carry unibz's 'Courses will definetely be starting' run-confirmation flag, which the sibling Master in Horticultural Science does carry. Given two signed ranking lists, a published 2026/27 catalogue with named lecturers and a September info session, this is a site-metadata gap rather than a substantive doubt — but it is a real discrepancy.
(v) The Late Application ranking list drops the 'only if there are study places still available' proviso from the late-enrolment sentence that both the admission PDF and the Early Bird list include. The restrictive version should be assumed to govern.
(vi) No language-exam sitting is scheduled for the Additional Application Session, even though the session is open to applicants who may need one.

DATA THAT DOES NOT EXIST YET, and its absence is itself information: no graduation-grade distribution, no AlmaLaurea employability or satisfaction statistics, no alumni, no published application counts (only admissions), no enrolment counts, no 2025/26 ranking lists retrievable at stable URLs, and no third-party review of the programme. Anyone comparing this master against an established one is comparing a prospectus with a track record.

Deadlines, quotas, scoring thresholds, certificate score bands, provincial grant amounts and ranking-list URLs change every cycle, and this programme is still being tuned between cohorts (a renamed course after one year). The 2026/27 non-EU window closed on 28/04/2026; the EU Additional Session closes 04/09/2026; 2027/28 dates are unpublished.
